sources.entry: Heimdall - Elegant solution to organise all your web applications. (Source Code) MIT PHP
Heimdall | Simple application dashboard for your web apps

summary.one_liner: Heimdall is a self-hosted web dashboard for organising links to your web applications, with optional live stats from supported apps and a configurable search bar.
summary.what_it_does: Heimdall is a PHP (Laravel 11) application that gives you a single page of tiles linking to your web apps, or to any other URL you choose. Foundation apps are recognised by title and get an icon and default tile colour filled in automatically. Enhanced apps connect to an app's API to show live stats on the dashboard, such as queue size and download speed for NZBGet and Sabnzbd. The dashboard can include a search bar that uses Google, Bing or DuckDuckGo, and it can be used as a browser start page. Search providers are customised through a searchproviders.yaml file, and a Tiles entry lets you search your own dashboard by app name. The app ships with translations for about 20 languages and a built-in setting that blocks server-side requests to private IP addresses unless explicitly enabled.
use_cases: organise links to self-hosted web applications
live download stats for NZBGet or Sabnzbd on a dashboard
landing page for home server apps
pin favourite links in one place
dashboard for internal services behind a reverse proxy
how_to_run: Alternatively, run the linuxserver.io Docker image (multi-arch: x86-64, armhf, arm64); the README links to instructions but does not include the commands.
notable: Enhanced apps show live API stats directly on the dashboard tiles
Supported apps are auto-filled by typing their title, which sets icon and colour
Search bar supports Google, Bing or DuckDuckGo, with customisable providers in YAML
Built-in SSRF protection that blocks private IP requests, with an ALLOW_INTERNAL_REQUESTS switch
Can run offline by hosting its own apps list (list.json)
caveats: Apache needs .htaccess allowed or the rewrite rules copied into the config; otherwise links such as /settings break
Background images over 2MB need upload_max_filesize raised in php.ini
Enhanced apps running in other Docker containers may need Docker network addresses, and self-signed certificates need extra CA configuration
